content.content: # Dolt is Git for Data! Dolt is a SQL database that you can fork, clone, branch, merge, push and pull just like a Git repository. Connect to Dolt just like any MySQL database to read or modify schema and data. Version control functionality is exposed in SQL via system tables, functions, and procedures. Or, use the Git-like command line interface to import CSV files, commit your changes, push them to a remote, or merge your teammate's changes. All the commands you know for Git work exactly the same for Dolt. Git versions files. Dolt versions tables. It's like Git and MySQL had a baby. We also built [DoltHub](https://www.dolthub.com), a place to share Dolt databases. We host public data for free. If you want to host your own version of DoltHub, we have [DoltLab](https://www.doltlab.com). If you want us to run a Dolt server for you, we have [Hosted Dolt](https://hosted.doltdb.com). Prefer Postgres instead of MySQL? Try [Doltgres](https://github.com/dolthub/doltgresql), now in its Beta release. [Join us on Discord](https://discord.com/invite/RFwfYpu) to say hi and ask questions, or [check out our roadmap](https://dolthub.com/docs/other/roadmap) to see what we're building next. # Video Introduction [![Dolt Explainer Video](https://img.youtube.com/vi/H2iZy0Cme10/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H2iZy0Cme10) # What's it for? Lots of things! Dolt is a generally useful tool with countless applications. But if you want some ideas, [here's how people are using it so far](https://dolthub.com/blog/2024-10-15-dolt-use-cases/).

1	# AGENT.md - Dolt Database Operations Guide
2	
3	This file provides guidance for AI agents working with Dolt databases to maximize productivity and follow best practices.
4	
5	## Quick Start
6	
7	Dolt is "Git for Data" - a SQL database with version control capabilities. All Git commands have Dolt equivalents:
8	- `git add` → `dolt add`  
9	- `git commit` → `dolt commit`
10	- `git branch` → `dolt branch`
11	- `git merge` → `dolt merge`
12	- `git diff` → `dolt diff`
13	
14	For help and documentation on commands, you can run `dolt --help` and `dolt <command> --help`.
15	
16	## Essential Dolt CLI Commands
17	
18	### Repository Operations
19	```bash
20	# Initialize new database
21	dolt init
22	
23	# Clone existing database
24	dolt clone <remote-url>
25	
26	# Show current status
27	dolt status
28	
29	# View commit history
30	dolt log
31	```
32	
33	### Branch Management
34	```bash
35	# List branches
36	dolt branch
37	
38	# Create new branch
39	dolt branch <branch-name>
40	
41	# Switch branches
42	dolt checkout <branch-name>
43	
44	# Create and switch to new branch
45	dolt checkout -b <branch-name>
46	```
47	
48	### Checkout Behavior with Running SQL Servers
49	- `dolt checkout` on the CLI only affects the shell process that runs the command. When a `dolt sql-server` is running, existing SQL connections keep their current branch until they explicitly switch.
50	- Each SQL session (CLI `dolt sql`, MySQL client, application connection) maintains its own active branch. Run `CALL dolt_checkout('<branch>');` at the beginning of every session or scripted block to ensure you are on the correct branch.
51	- Chain branch changes inside scripts: start with `CALL dolt_checkout('<branch>');`, then run your queries. Do not assume a previous checkout persists for new connections.
52	- When automating, include the checkout in the same transaction / session context where the data changes execute.
53	- A good way to make sure a `dolt sql` session connects to the br1 branch for instance is `dolt --branch br1 sql`.
54	
55	### Data Operations
56	```bash
57	# Stage changes
58	dolt add <table-name>
59	dolt add .  # stage all changes
60	
61	# Commit changes
62	dolt commit -m "commit message"
63	
64	# View differences
65	dolt diff
66	dolt diff <table-name>
67	dolt diff <branch1> <branch2>
68	
69	# Merge branches
70	dolt merge <branch-name>
71	```
72	
73	## Starting and Connecting to Dolt SQL Server
74	
75	### Start SQL Server
76	```bash
77	# Start server on default port (3306)
78	dolt sql-server
79	
80	# Start on specific port
81	dolt sql-server --port=3307
82	
83	# Start with specific host
84	dolt sql-server --host=0.0.0.0 --port=3307
85	
86	# Start in background
87	dolt sql-server --port=3307 &
88	```
89	
90	### Connecting to SQL Server
91	```bash
92	# Connect with dolt sql command
93	dolt sql
94	
95	# Connect with mysql client
96	mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -u root
97	
98	# Connect with specific database
99	mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 3306 -u root -D <database-name>
100	```
101	
102	## Dolt Testing with dolt_test System Table
103	
104	### Unit Testing with dolt_test
105	
106	The dolt_test system table provides a powerful way to create and run unit tests for your database. This is the preferred method for testing data integrity, business rules, and schema validation.
107	
108	#### Creating Tests
109	
110	Tests are created by inserting rows into the `dolt_tests` system table:
111	
112	```sql
113	-- Create a simple test
114	INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
115	    'test_user_count', 
116	    'validation', 
117	    'SELECT COUNT(*) as user_count FROM users;', 
118	    'row_count',
119	    '>',
120	    '0'
121	);
122	
123	-- Create a test with expected result
124	INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
125	    'test_valid_emails', 
126	    'validation', 
127	    'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE email NOT LIKE "%@%";', 
128	    'row_count',
129	    '==',
130	    '0'
131	);
132	
133	-- Create a schema validation test
134	INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
135	    'test_users_schema', 
136	    'schema', 
137	    'DESCRIBE users;', 
138	    'row_count',
139	    '>=',
140	    '5'
141	);
142	```
143	
144	#### Test Structure
145	
146	Each test row contains:
147	- test_name: Unique identifier for the test
148	- test_group: Optional grouping for tests (e.g., 'validation', 'schema', 'integration')
149	- test_query: SQL query to execute
150	- assertion_type: Type of assertion ('expected_rows', 'expected_columns', 'expected_single_value')
151	- assertion_comparator: Comparison operator ('==', '>', '<', '>=', '<=', '!=')
152	- assertion_value: Expected value for comparison
153	
154	#### Running Tests
155	
156	```sql
157	-- Run all tests
158	SELECT * FROM dolt_test_run();
159	
160	-- Run specific test
161	SELECT * FROM dolt_test_run('test_user_count');
162	
163	-- Run tests with filtering
164	SELECT * FROM dolt_test_run() WHERE test_name LIKE 'test_user%' AND status != 'PASS';
165	```
166	
167	#### Test Result Interpretation
168	
169	The dolt_test_run() function returns:
170	- test_name: Name of the test
171	- status: PASS, FAIL, or ERROR
172	- actual_result: Actual query result
173	- expected_result: Expected result
174	- message: Additional details
175	
176	#### Advanced Testing Examples
177	
178	```sql
179	-- Test data integrity
180	INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
181	    'test_no_orphaned_orders', 
182	    'integrity', 
183	    'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o LEFT JOIN users u ON o.user_id = u.id WHERE u.id IS NULL;', 
184	    'row_count',
185	    '==',
186	    '0'
187	);
188	
189	-- Test business rules
190	INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
191	    'test_positive_prices', 
192	    'business_rules', 
193	    'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE price <= 0;', 
194	    'row_count',
195	    '==',
196	    '0'
197	);
198	
199	-- Test complex relationships
200	INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
201	    'test_order_totals', 
202	    'integrity', 
203	    'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.price) != o.total;', 
204	    'row_count',
205	    '==',
206	    '0'
207	);
208	```
209	
210	### Dolt CI for DoltHub Integration
211	
212	Dolt CI is specifically designed for running tests on DoltHub when pull requests are created. Use this only for tests you want to run automatically on DoltHub.
213	
214	#### Prerequisites for DoltHub CI
215	- Requires Dolt v1.43.14 or later
216	- Must initialize CI capabilities: `dolt ci init`
217	- Workflows defined in YAML files
218	
219	#### Available CI Commands
220	```bash
221	# Initialize CI capabilities
222	dolt ci init
223	
224	# List available workflows
225	dolt ci ls
226	
227	# View workflow details
228	dolt ci view <workflow-name>
229	
230	# View specific job in workflow
231	dolt ci view <workflow-name> <job-name>
232	
233	# Run workflow locally (for testing before DoltHub)
234	dolt ci run <workflow-name>
235	```
236	
237	#### Creating CI Workflows for DoltHub
238	
239	Create workflow files that will run on DoltHub when pull requests are opened:
240	
241	```yaml
242	name: doltHub validation workflow
243	on:
244	  push:
245	    branches:
246	      - master
247	      - main
248	jobs:
249	  - name: validate schema
250	    steps:
251	      - name: check required tables exist
252	        saved_query_name: show_tables
253	        expected_rows: ">= 3"
254	      
255	      - name: validate user data
256	        saved_query_name: user_count_check
257	        expected_columns: "== 1"
258	        expected_rows: "> 0"
259	  
260	  - name: data integrity checks
261	    steps:
262	      - name: check email format
263	        saved_query_name: valid_emails
264	        expected_rows: "== 0"  # No invalid emails
265	```
266	
267	### Best Practices for Testing
268	
269	1. **Use dolt_test for Unit Testing**
270	   - Create tests for data validation
271	   - Test business rules and constraints
272	   - Validate schema changes
273	   - Run tests frequently during development
274	
275	2. **Use Dolt CI for DoltHub Integration**
276	   - Only for tests that should run on pull requests
277	   - Focus on integration and deployment validation
278	   - Test against production-like data
279	
280	3. **Create Comprehensive Test Suites**
281	   - Test data integrity constraints
282	   - Validate business rules
283	   - Check schema requirements
284	   - Verify data relationships
285	
286	4. **Version Control Your Tests**
287	   - Commit test definitions to repository
288	   - Track changes to test configuration
289	   - Use branches for test development
290	
291	## System Tables for Version Control
292	
293	Dolt exposes version control operations through system tables accessible via SQL:
294	
295	### Core System Tables
296	```sql
297	-- View commit history
298	SELECT * FROM dolt_log;
299	
300	-- Check current status
301	SELECT * FROM dolt_status;
302	
303	-- View branch information
304	SELECT * FROM dolt_branches;
305	
306	-- See table diffs
307	SELECT * FROM dolt_diff_<table_name>;
308	
309	-- View schema changes
310	SELECT * FROM dolt_schema_diff;
311	
312	-- Check conflicts during merge
313	SELECT * FROM dolt_conflicts_<table_name>;
314	
315	-- View commit metadata
316	SELECT * FROM dolt_commits;
317	```
318	
319	### Version Control Operations via SQL
320	
321	When working in SQL sessions, you can execute version control operations using stored procedures:
322	
323	```sql
324	-- Stage and commit changes
325	CALL dolt_add('.');
326	CALL dolt_commit('-m', 'commit message');
327	
328	-- Branch operations
329	CALL dolt_branch('<branch_name>');
330	CALL dolt_checkout('<branch_name>');
331	CALL dolt_merge('<branch_name>');
332	```
333	
334	**Note:** Use CLI commands (`dolt add`, `dolt commit`, etc.) for most operations. SQL procedures are useful when already in a SQL session.
335	
336	### Advanced System Tables
337	```sql
338	-- View remotes
339	SELECT * FROM dolt_remotes;
340	
341	-- Check merge conflicts
342	SELECT * FROM dolt_conflicts;
343	
344	-- View statistics
345	SELECT * FROM dolt_statistics;
346	
347	-- See ignored tables
348	SELECT * FROM dolt_ignore;
349	```
350	
351	## CLI vs SQL Approach
352	
353	**Prefer CLI commands for:**
354	- Version control operations (add, commit, branch, merge)
355	- Repository management (init, clone, push, pull)
356	- Conflict resolution
357	- Status checking and history viewing
358	
359	**Use SQL for:**
360	- Data queries and analysis
361	- Complex data transformations
362	- Examining system tables (dolt_log, dolt_status, etc.)
363	- When already in an active SQL session
364	
365	## Schema Design Recommendations
366	
367	### Use UUID Keys Instead of Auto-Increment
368	
369	For Dolt's version control features, use UUID primary keys instead of auto-increment:
370	
371	```sql
372	-- Recommended
373	CREATE TABLE users (
374	    id varchar(36) default(uuid()) primary key,
375	    name varchar(255)
376	);
377	
378	-- Avoid auto-increment with Dolt
379	-- id int auto_increment primary key
380	```
381	
382	**Benefits:**
383	- Prevents merge conflicts across branches and database clones
384	- Automatic generation with default(uuid())
385	- Works seamlessly in distributed environments
386	
387	## Best Practices for Agents
388	
389	### 1. Always Work on Feature Branches
390	```bash
391	# Create feature branch before making changes
392	dolt checkout -b feature/agent-changes
393	
394	# Make changes on feature branch
395	dolt sql -q "INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'Alice');"
396	
397	# Stage and commit
398	dolt add .
399	dolt commit -m "Add new user Alice"
400	
401	# Switch back to main to merge
402	dolt checkout main
403	dolt merge feature/agent-changes
404	```
405	
406	### 2. Use SQL for Data Operations, CLI for Version Control
407	```bash
408	# Use dolt sql for data changes
409	dolt sql -q "INSERT INTO users VALUES (1, 'Alice');"
410	dolt sql -q "UPDATE products SET price = price * 1.1 WHERE category = 'electronics';"
411	
412	# Check status and commit using CLI
413	dolt status
414	dolt add .
415	dolt commit -m "Update user and product data"
416	```
417	
418	### 3. Validate Changes with System Tables
419	```sql
420	-- Before major operations, check current state
421	SELECT * FROM dolt_status;
422	SELECT * FROM dolt_branches;
423	
424	-- After changes, verify with diffs
425	SELECT * FROM dolt_diff_users;
426	SELECT * FROM dolt_schema_diff;
427	```
428	
429	### 4. Use dolt_test for Data Validation
430	Create tests to validate:
431	- Data integrity after changes
432	- Schema compatibility
433	- Business rule compliance
434	- Cross-table relationships
435	
436	### 5. Handle Conflicts Gracefully
437	```bash
438	# Check for conflicts using CLI
439	dolt conflicts cat <table_name>
440	dolt conflicts resolve --ours <table_name>
441	dolt conflicts resolve --theirs <table_name>
442	
443	# Or use SQL to examine conflicts
444	dolt sql -q "SELECT * FROM dolt_conflicts_<table_name>;"
445	```
446	
447	## Common Workflow Examples
448	
449	### Data Migration Workflow
450	```bash
451	# Create migration branch
452	dolt checkout -b migration/update-schema
453	
454	# Apply schema changes via SQL
455	dolt sql -q "ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN email VARCHAR(255);"
456	
457	# Create validation tests
458	dolt sql -q "INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES ('test_users_schema', 'schema', 'DESCRIBE users;', 'row_count', '>=', '6');"
459	dolt sql -q "INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES ('test_email_column', 'schema', 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE email IS NULL;', 'row_count', '>=', '0');"
460	
461	# Run tests to validate changes
462	dolt sql -q "SELECT * FROM dolt_test_run();"
463	
464	# Stage and commit
465	dolt add .
466	dolt commit -m "Add email column to users table"
467	
468	# Merge back
469	dolt checkout main
470	dolt merge migration/update-schema
471	```
472	
473	### Data Analysis Workflow
474	```bash
475	# Create analysis branch
476	dolt checkout -b analysis/user-behavior
477	
478	# Create analysis tables via SQL
479	dolt sql -q "CREATE TABLE user_metrics AS 
480	            SELECT user_id, COUNT(*) as actions 
481	            FROM user_actions 
482	            GROUP BY user_id;"
483	
484	# Create tests to validate analysis
485	dolt sql -q "INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES ('test_metrics_created', 'analysis', 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_metrics;', 'row_count', '>', '0');"
486	dolt sql -q "INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES ('test_metrics_integrity', 'integrity', 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM user_metrics um LEFT JOIN users u ON um.user_id = u.id WHERE u.id IS NULL;', 'row_count', '==', '0');"
487	
488	# Run tests to validate analysis
489	dolt sql -q "SELECT * FROM dolt_test_run();"
490	
491	# Stage and commit using CLI
492	dolt add user_metrics
493	dolt commit -m "Add user behavior analysis"
494	```
495	
496	## Integration with External Tools
497	
498	### Database Clients
499	Most MySQL clients work with Dolt:
500	- MySQL Workbench
501	- phpMyAdmin  
502	- DataGrip
503	- DBeaver
504	
505	### Backup and Sync
506	```bash
507	# Push to remote
508	dolt push origin main
509	
510	# Pull changes
511	dolt pull origin main
512	
513	# Clone for backup
514	dolt clone <remote-url> backup-location
515	```
516	
517	This guide enables agents to leverage Dolt's unique version control capabilities while maintaining data integrity and following collaborative development practices.

# AGENT.md - Dolt Database Operations Guide

This file provides guidance for AI agents working with Dolt databases to maximize productivity and follow best practices.

## Quick Start

Dolt is "Git for Data" - a SQL database with version control capabilities. All Git commands have Dolt equivalents:
- `git add` → `dolt add`  
- `git commit` → `dolt commit`
- `git branch` → `dolt branch`
- `git merge` → `dolt merge`
- `git diff` → `dolt diff`

For help and documentation on commands, you can run `dolt --help` and `dolt <command> --help`.

## Essential Dolt CLI Commands

### Repository Operations
```bash
# Initialize new database
dolt init

# Clone existing database
dolt clone <remote-url>

# Show current status
dolt status

# View commit history
dolt log
```

### Branch Management
```bash
# List branches
dolt branch

# Create new branch
dolt branch <branch-name>

# Switch branches
dolt checkout <branch-name>

# Create and switch to new branch
dolt checkout -b <branch-name>
```

### Checkout Behavior with Running SQL Servers
- `dolt checkout` on the CLI only affects the shell process that runs the command. When a `dolt sql-server` is running, existing SQL connections keep their current branch until they explicitly switch.
- Each SQL session (CLI `dolt sql`, MySQL client, application connection) maintains its own active branch. Run `CALL dolt_checkout('<branch>');` at the beginning of every session or scripted block to ensure you are on the correct branch.
- Chain branch changes inside scripts: start with `CALL dolt_checkout('<branch>');`, then run your queries. Do not assume a previous checkout persists for new connections.
- When automating, include the checkout in the same transaction / session context where the data changes execute.
- A good way to make sure a `dolt sql` session connects to the br1 branch for instance is `dolt --branch br1 sql`.

### Data Operations
```bash
# Stage changes
dolt add <table-name>
dolt add .  # stage all changes

# Commit changes
dolt commit -m "commit message"

# View differences
dolt diff
dolt diff <table-name>
dolt diff <branch1> <branch2>

# Merge branches
```

## Dolt Testing with dolt_test System Table

### Unit Testing with dolt_test

The dolt_test system table provides a powerful way to create and run unit tests for your database. This is the preferred method for testing data integrity, business rules, and schema validation.

#### Creating Tests

Tests are created by inserting rows into the `dolt_tests` system table:

```sql
-- Create a simple test
INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
    'test_user_count', 
    'validation', 
    'SELECT COUNT(*) as user_count FROM users;', 
    'row_count',
    '>',
    '0'
);

-- Create a test with expected result
INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
    'test_valid_emails', 
    'validation', 
    'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE email NOT LIKE "%@%";', 
    'row_count',
    '==',
    '0'
);

-- Create a schema validation test
INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
    'test_users_schema', 
    'schema', 
    'DESCRIBE users;', 
    'row_count',
    '>=',
    '5'
);
```

#### Test Structure

Each test row contains:
- test_name: Unique identifier for the test
- test_group: Optional grouping for tests (e.g., 'validation', 'schema', 'integration')
- test_query: SQL query to execute
- assertion_type: Type of assertion ('expected_rows', 'expected_columns', 'expected_single_value')
- assertion_comparator: Comparison operator ('==', '>', '<', '>=', '<=', '!=')
- assertion_value: Expected value for comparison

#### Running Tests

```sql
-- Run all tests
SELECT * FROM dolt_test_run();

-- Run specific test
SELECT * FROM dolt_test_run('test_user_count');

-- Run tests with filtering
SELECT * FROM dolt_test_run() WHERE test_name LIKE 'test_user%' AND status != 'PASS';
```

#### Test Result Interpretation

The dolt_test_run() function returns:
- test_name: Name of the test
- status: PASS, FAIL, or ERROR
- actual_result: Actual query result
- expected_result: Expected result
- message: Additional details

#### Advanced Testing Examples

```sql
-- Test data integrity
INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
    'test_no_orphaned_orders', 
    'integrity', 
    'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o LEFT JOIN users u ON o.user_id = u.id WHERE u.id IS NULL;', 
    'row_count',
    '==',
    '0'
);

-- Test business rules
INSERT INTO `dolt_tests` VALUES (
    'test_positive_prices', 
    'business_rules', 
    'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM products WHERE price <= 0;', 
    'row_count',
    '==',
    '0'
);

-- Test complex relationships

    'test_order_totals', 
    'integrity', 
    'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.id = oi.order_id GROUP BY o.id HAVING SUM(oi.quantity * oi.price) != o.total;', 
    'row_count',
    '==',
    '0'
);
```

Dolt CI is specifically designed for running tests on DoltHub when pull requests are created. Use this only for tests you want to run automatically on DoltHub.

```yaml
name: doltHub validation workflow
```

## System Tables for Version Control

Dolt exposes version control operations through system tables accessible via SQL:

When working in SQL sessions, you can execute version control operations using stored procedures:

```sql
CALL dolt_branch('<branch_name>');
CALL dolt_checkout('<branch_name>');
```

**Prefer CLI commands for:**

**Use SQL for:**
- Data queries and analysis
- Complex data transformations

### Use UUID Keys Instead of Auto-Increment

For Dolt's version control features, use UUID primary keys instead of auto-increment:

```sql
    name varchar(255)
);
```

**Benefits:**
- Prevents merge conflicts across branches and database clones
- Automatic generation with default(uuid())
- Works seamlessly in distributed environments

## Step 1 — Orientation

**Project.** Dolt is "Git for Data" — a MySQL-compatible SQL database with Git-style version control, written in Go. All code lives under `go/`, one module (`go/go.mod`).

**Layout.**

## Step 2 — Storage lifecycle contract (root tracking, swap, layers to disk)

The storage root is a single `hash.Hash` (the address of the noms dataset map). It is **read**, **swapped atomically**, and **re-synced**, all delegated down the layer stack:

| Layer | file:line | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `DoltDB.NomsRoot` | `doltdb/doltdb.go:239` | reads current root — `ChunkStoreFromDatabase(ddb.db).Root(ctx)` |
| `DoltDB.CommitRoot` | `doltdb/doltdb.go:248` | **the swap** — `ChunkStore.Commit(ctx, current, last)`, atomic CAS of the manifest root |
| `DoltDB.writeRootValue` / `doWriteRootValue` | `doltdb/doltdb.go:807`, `:826` | serializes a `RootValue` into chunks before the root moves |
| `datas.Database.chunkStore()` | `store/datas/database.go:180`; accessor `ChunkStoreFromDatabase` `:221` | the seam from the dataset DB down to raw chunk storage |
| `types.ValueStore.cs` | `store/types/value_store.go:76` | value (de)serialization over a `chunks.ChunkStore` |
| `tree.NodeStore.store` | `store/prolly/tree/node_store.go:66` | prolly-tree node access over the same `chunks.ChunkStore` |
| `chunks.ChunkStore` interface | `store/chunks/chunk_store.go:74` — `Root` `:111`, `Commit` `:116`, `Rebase` `:107` | the storage contract: read root, CAS root, resync to persisted root |
| `nbs.GenerationalNBS` | `store/nbs/generational_chunk_store.go:40`, `Root:307`, `Commit:314` | old-gen + new-gen split store; routes root ops to new-gen |
| `nbs.NomsBlockStore` | `store/nbs/store.go:96` | concrete store; root lives in `manifest` (`:98`) & `upstream manifestContents` (`:121`); `Root:1548`, `Commit:1558` |

**Contract in one line:** everything above `chunks.ChunkStore` treats the root as opaque and immutable-per-open; the root only moves through `ChunkStore.Commit(current,last)`, and a store learns of an external move only via `Rebase`. Any long-lived holder that cached a `RootValue`/`Commit`/root hash — or a `ValueStore`/`NodeStore`/`Database`/`ChunkStore` handle — is pinned to the root as of its open and is what a rework can silently strand.

## Step 3 — How query access is handed out

1. **Ask.** A command builds/loads a `DoltEnv` and calls `DoltEnv.DoltDB(ctx)` (`env/environment.go:119`) or `DoltEnv.DbData(ctx)` (`env/environment.go:929`), packaging the handle as `env.DbData{Ddb,...}` (`env/repo_state.go:60`).
2. **Construct the SQL face.** `sqle.NewDatabase(ctx, name, dbData, editOpts)` (`sqle/database.go:203`) stores `dbData.Ddb` into `Database.ddb` (`sqle/database.go:80`).
3. **Register in provider.** `DoltDatabaseProvider.databases map[string]dsess.SqlDatabase` (`sqle/database_provider.go:75`) holds each DB behind the **narrow `dsess.SqlDatabase` interface** (never naming `Database`/`DoltDB`).
4. **Session.** `NewDoltSession` (`dsess/session.go:102`) → `DoltSession.provider` (`session.go:49`).
5. **Lookup on query.** `DoltDatabaseProvider.Database(ctx,name)` (`database_provider.go:396`) returns a `sql.Database`; consumers recover the handle via `db.(dsess.SqlDatabase).DbData().Ddb` (`sqle/database.go:296`).
6. **Retain for later.** Session-scoped: `DoltSession.dbStates` → `DatabaseSessionState` (`dsess/database_session_state.go:61`) → `branchState.dbData env.DbData` (`database_session_state.go:100`); and `DoltSession.dbCache` → `DatabaseCache.revisionDbs map[...]SqlDatabase` (`dsess/session_cache.go:63`).
